answer: Each identity must post a non-refundable staked deposit to earn standing. A Sybil attacker with a thousand wallets locks real capital in every one, so the cost of the next fake identity stays flat rather than collapsing toward zero. Honest agents reclaim their stake on exit; a clone farm cannot, since it funds all copies at once or exposes itself paying them in sequence. Weight scales with stake, not headcount, so capturing a round costs about as much as buying the outcome. Slow unbonding also blocks stake feeding a fresh spiral of accounts, so the oasis a forger seeks stays past the horizon.
